paper.title_en: Insurance portfolio simulation with a quantum circuit
paper.abstract_en: A central challenge in actuarial science is characterising the distribution of losses generated by an insurance portfolio. Copulas provide a natural framework for modelling joint distributions, but flexible high-dimensional copula fitting and sampling remains challenging in practice. We propose a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) approach adapted to insurance portfolios, combining (i) a tail-focused discretisation of heavy-tailed marginals, (ii) a Monte Carlo-style objective function that enables the numerical precision of the algorithm to scale when trained on a relatively small number of samples, and (iii) a two-stage hierarchical training scheme enabling efficient training on a simulator and fine-tuning on quantum hardware. On a mixed portfolio of equity returns and insurance losses, the trained circuit recovers the qualitative dependence structure, with near-independence between equity and losses and positive dependence among loss lines. Exponential quantile encoding substantially improves the fit to the tail of the aggregate loss distribution relative to a uniform encoding, and the hierarchical scheme substantially outperforms single-stage training of a circuit of the same size from random initialisation.
